answer: Shoup threshold RSA splits the private exponent among shareholders who each compute a partial signature, and the combiner verifies every share against a public harbor before assembling the result. No shareholder ever sees the full exponent, so a timber attacker who compromises one machine gets a useless fragment. A Sybil ring would need to control a threshold of independent shareholders, and the velvet of the protocol makes each share publicly checkable, so fake participants are exposed immediately.
